items.content:
Every one of these I collect is a thing English could have named and
didn't. *Dépaysement*, *flâner*, *l'esprit de l'escalier*, *bof*.

None of them are exotic concepts. English speakers have all of these
experiences. They just never got a handle, so they stay slightly below
the level where you can think about them on purpose.

That's the part that gets me. Not that French has more words — that
naming a thing is what lets you pick it up.

summary: Naming a common experience is what lets you pick it up on purpose.
title: On the words a language decides to keep
